ticket: The service is noticeably slow during our afternoon peak and fine the rest of the day. We have autoscaling enabled so I expected it to cope.
reply:
This reply was drafted automatically from our documentation. Reply to this message to reach a person.

One common cause of elevated latency is that the instance count is not scaling with the load pattern. [DOC-PERF-001] You should compare median and 95th percentile latency on the metrics page; a large gap indicates contention or queueing. [DOC-PERF-001] Check memory utilisation across instances; sustained utilisation above eighty per cent can cause latency before failures appear. [DOC-PERF-001] Review the dependency timing breakdown on the trace view to see if time is spent in your service or a downstream dependency. [DOC-PERF-001] Verify that the service is not already at its configured maximum instance count, as scaling stops there regardless of load. [DOC-PERF-002] Consider adjusting the autoscaling policy to use a faster‑responding metric such as request count and set a minimum instance count above zero for latency‑sensitive services. [DOC-PERF-002]

ticket:
Need to roll back the latest release
How do I revert to an earlier revision? The release we put out this morning is causing errors and I would rather roll back than try to fix forward.
reply:
This reply was drafted automatically from our documentation. Reply to this message to reach a person.

A release has introduced errors and must be reverted. [DOC-DEPLOY-002] Open the revisions page for the service and identify the last revision that was healthy. [DOC-DEPLOY-002] Select roll back on that revision; traffic moves within roughly thirty seconds and no rebuild takes place. [DOC-DEPLOY-002] If the release included a database migration, roll the migration back before the service, or the older code will encounter a schema it does not expect. [DOC-DEPLOY-002] Record the incident and the reason for the rollback before deploying a fix. [DOC-DEPLOY-002] Rollback restores the container image and its configuration together, but does not restore data. [DOC-DEPLOY-002]

ticket:
How do I page through large results
when i do pagination some record coming two time and some missing. what is correct way?
reply:
This reply was drafted automatically from our documentation. Reply to this message to reach a person.

Iterating through results can miss or duplicate records. [DOC-API-002] This can happen if the cursor from the previous response was not passed to the next request, if offset pagination was used against a changing collection, or if the page size requested exceeds the maximum. [DOC-API-002] Use cursor pagination for anything that may change while you iterate. [DOC-API-002] Pass the next_cursor value from each response as the cursor parameter of the following request, and stop when it is null. [DOC-API-002] Keep page size at or below two hundred. [DOC-API-002] Cursors expire after one hour; long‑running iterations should handle expiry by restarting from a recorded checkpoint. [DOC-API-002]

Sources:
- [DOC-API-002] Pagination and handling large result sets
